title: What is Consumerism?
description: Luyện nghe và học từ vựng IELTS qua chủ đề Kinh tế - Xã hội: Nguồn gốc, tác động và bản chất của Chủ nghĩa tiêu dùng (Consumerism).
transcript:
In this Modern Age developed Nations have access to products that have truly changed Society from the smartphone the TV to items we take as ___necessities___ today like a refrigerator it can feel like the whole world is looking to what's next a mentality based around buying that circulates everywhere this idea is known as ___consumerism___ the idea that buying items ___fulfills___ a purpose rather than just what's needed. This video doesn't intend to necessarily call out consumerism as an objective good or bad but instead look to where its roots lie where it is now and what role it plays in Modern Life.

Humanity always desires more whether it be power wealth property or just influence humans want more. This concept isn't new as even in ancient times some would have far more than others usually based around positions in society. As Society developed the wealthy began to ___flaunt___ their wealth with ___possessions___ fancy clothes numerous spices hiring servants and so on. This was ___reserved___ for the top tiers of society until just a century ago when the concepts of ___mass production___ and ___interchangeable___ parts allowed even unskilled workers to produce highquality products in ___bulk___. The price of these Goods became cheap enough that a quickly ___expanding___ middle class could soon purchase items once considered well Out Of Reach.

These new items developed a new mindset amongst both the middle class and upper class alike to always acquire more. For some context before this expansion of consumerism goods were purchased with specific ___intent___ whether this was to make work easier or a necessity to live goods were purchased when needed and rarely more. As consumerism hit the mainstream people desired new Goods constantly. This concept was greatly explored by sociologist thir Vin he created the idea of ___conspicuous___ consumption the ___acquisition___ of expensive Goods created the ___perception___ of wealth and success a fancy watch a new car air conditioning and more showed off that the owner must be well off clothes were not the only way to determine the success of a stranger now their possessions did all of the talking for them.

As more people desired to be admired for possessions and the perception of success that came with it they wanted to buy more. This made marketing team's jobs far easier as they could Market towards the expanding middle class making new non-essential items seem like a must. The line between need and want begins to ___blur___ and over the decades consumerism becomes so ___ingrained___ in the human consciousness that it becomes hard to escape.

As time went on media and artists became ___commercialized___ using advertisements as these industries such as film grew so did the desire put advertisements before and sometimes during them. An average TV show consists of around 9 minutes of advertisements for every 30 minutes or around 30% of a program. As this becomes the new National Pastime so to speak more Brands become recognizable and developed in image as more products become part of common knowledge it made the idea of owning that product even more appealing. Marketing budgets began to ___surpass___ the actual production of the product and eventually we arrive to where we are at today.

Consumerism sounds pretty bad right constant advertisements a desire for more being the mentality of so many but in ___actuality___ it really isn't all that bad. Without consumerism companies lose a drive to compete with not just other companies but the consumer's interest. Sometimes this involves making a better product and sometimes it can allow a small creative mind to sell a product without everybody saying why do I need this. Consumerism gives Merit to what some would see as pointless products looking at you Smartwatch while ___simultaneously___ giving those who wanted the opportunity to buy it. Of course the negatives of consumerism are Apparent at every turn success isn't determined by how many cars you have or how big your TV is it just shows how you choose to spend your money not always bad not always good but it's something you and I will just have to deal with. This is Cody of Knowledge Hub.

vocabulary.meaning: Nhu yếu phẩm, thứ thiết yếu
vocabulary.example: In modern society, access to clean water is considered a basic necessity.
Shift in consumer mentality has led to an increased demand for eco-friendly products.
Modern consumerism encourages individuals to buy goods far beyond their actual needs.
Misleading advertisements often circulate widely on social media platforms.

vocabulary.meaning: Đạt được, đáp ứng (mục đích/nhu cầu)
vocabulary.example: Purchasing luxury items rarely fulfills long-term psychological needs.
Wealthy individuals often flaunt their riches through expensive clothing and accessories.
Material possessions do not necessarily guarantee personal satisfaction.
High-end sports cars were once reserved exclusively for the upper tier of society.
The rise of mass production drastically reduced the price of household goods.

vocabulary.meaning: Có thể thay thế cho nhau
vocabulary.example: Interchangeable parts allowed factories to assemble complex machines quickly and cheaply.
Buying goods in bulk helps consumers save a significant amount of money.
The rapidly expanding middle class drove economic growth throughout the twentieth century.
Before the modern era, tools were bought with the specific intent of completing work efficiently.
Conspicuous consumption occurs when people purchase goods primarily to project high social status.

vocabulary.meaning: Sự mua lại, sự sở hữu
vocabulary.example: The acquisition of expensive jewelry created a strong perception of success.
Public perception of a brand is heavily influenced by targeted advertising campaigns.
During economic recessions, households tend to cut back on non-essential items.
Constant marketing has served to blur the distinction between absolute needs and mere wants.
Shopping habits have become deeply ingrained in the modern human consciousness.
Major holidays have become highly commercialized over recent decades.

vocabulary.meaning: Trò tiêu khiển quốc gia / thói quen phổ biến
vocabulary.example: Watching television eventually became the dominant national pastime for millions.
Marketing budgets now frequently surpass the actual costs of manufacturing the product.
While consumerism sounds negative, in actuality it drives corporate competition and innovation.
Tech companies must continuously innovate to compete effectively in a global market.
Some critics dismiss smartwatches as pointless gadgets, while others find them essential.
Online platforms allow businesses to reach global audiences simultaneously.
The environmental drawbacks of excessive resource use are becoming increasingly apparent.
Environmental awareness is slowly taking root in the public consciousness.
Advertisers heavily target younger demographics through digital social media campaigns.
Consumer demand provides merit to niche products that would otherwise lack a market.

mcqQuestions.q: What is the central definition of "consumerism" presented at the beginning of the video?
options: The economic requirement of purchasing only essential items for survival.
The idea that buying items fulfills a purpose rather than just satisfying what is needed.
A law requiring corporations to lower product prices for low-income workers.
The complete rejection of modern technology like TVs and smartphones.

mcqQuestions.q: According to the speaker, what historically enabled the middle class to purchase items once reserved for the wealthy?
options: Government subsidies distributed to all households.
Mass production and the use of interchangeable parts reducing prices.
A sudden drop in global population levels.
The elimination of all international trade tariffs.

mcqQuestions.q: How were goods typically purchased before the widespread expansion of consumerism?
options: Purely for display and social prestige.
Based on impulse decisions triggered by social media.
With specific intent, such as making work easier or serving as a vital necessity.
Through online credit platforms and monthly payment plans.

mcqQuestions.q: What does Thorstein Veblen's concept of "conspicuous consumption" explain?
options: Buying expensive goods to create a perception of wealth and personal success.
Hiding one's possessions to avoid paying higher taxes.
Manufacturing products using low-cost synthetic materials.
Recycling old tools to prevent economic waste.

mcqQuestions.q: "The line between need and want begins to blur..." What does this sentence mean?
options: Essential goods become completely unavailable in retail stores.
Effective marketing makes non-essential items feel like absolute necessities to consumers.
People stop purchasing both essential and luxury products.
Government regulations define exact limits on consumer spending.

mcqQuestions.q: Why did advertising expand so rapidly in media like television?
options: TV networks were legally forced to air advertisements by government mandate.
Ads funded growing media industries, taking up about 30% of standard programming time.
Viewers specifically requested more advertisements during broadcasts.
TV production costs dropped to zero due to sponsorship.

mcqQuestions.q: What positive aspect of consumerism does Cody point out?
options: It eliminates all financial debt for average households.
It drives companies to compete, improve products, and give merit to niche creative ideas.
It guarantees that all manufactured goods last a lifetime.
It stops companies from spending money on marketing.

mcqQuestions.q: "Marketing budgets began to surpass the actual production of the product..."
options: Companies spend more money promoting a product than actually making it.
Manufacturing products has become too expensive for modern brands.
Advertisements are no longer profitable for corporations.
Products are given away for free because advertising covers all costs.

mcqQuestions.q: What does Cody suggest about products like smartwatches?
options: They are mandatory items that every citizen must own.
Consumerism provides a market opportunity for items some might see as pointless while allowing people the freedom to buy them.
They are the primary cause of global financial instability.
They were invented in ancient times by upper-tier rulers.

mcqQuestions.q: What is the main concluding stance of the video regarding consumerism?
options: Consumerism is an absolute evil that must be destroyed immediately.
Consumerism is a flawless system with zero drawbacks.
Consumerism has both clear negatives and positives, and it is a reality modern society must deal with.
Success in life is strictly measured by the number of cars a person owns.
